rationale: The primary clinical cohort study establishing autosomal dominant intellectual developmental disorder-77 (MRD77, OMIM #621415) by Willim et al. (2024) delineates 33 individuals harboring heterozygous pathogenic variants in LRRC7. Across this definitive multicenter cohort and subsequent single-case/CNV reports, intellectual disability and speech/language impairment represent the invariant hallmark neurodevelopmental manifestations, whereas neurobehavioral anomalies including autism spectrum traits, ADHD, and aggressive outbursts occur in variable subsets, consistent with the hypothesized core versus secondary syndromic architecture.

evidence.text: Willim et al. (2024) reported a multicenter cohort of 33 individuals with heterozygous missense or loss-of-function variants in LRRC7 presenting with a neurodevelopmental disorder characterized by intellectual disability and delayed language development as core phenotypic findings, with autism, ADHD, aggression, and hyperphagia observed across variable subsets.

source.title: Variants in LRRC7 lead to intellectual disability, autism, aggression and abnormal eating behaviors
source.quote: We identify here 33 individuals (one of them previously described) with a dominant neurodevelopmental disorder due to heterozygous missense or loss-of-function variants in LRRC7. The clinical spectrum involves intellectual disability, autism, ADHD, aggression and, in several cases, hyperphagia-associated obesity.

numbers.metric: Cohort size (individuals with dominant LRRC7 variants)

evidence.text: Khan et al. (2026) described an individual with a novel de novo heterozygous LRRC7 missense variant presenting with global developmental delay, moderate intellectual disability, language impairment, seizures, hypotonia, and microcephaly, further supporting that cognitive impairment and language deficit form the core clinical presentation.

source.title: Further Evidence for LRRC7 Gene Involvement in Neurodevelopmental Disorder: A Novel Variant
source.quote: Here, we investigated a proband presenting global developmental delay (GDD), tonic seizures, failure to thrive, mild microcephaly, intellectual disability (ID), and hypotonia... evidence.text: Tassano et al. (2015) identified a de novo 1p31 deletion affecting LRRC7 in a patient characterized specifically by intellectual disability and severe expressive and receptive language delay.

new_directions.question_text: What are the exact comparative penetrance frequencies of hyperphagia, childhood aggression, and sleep disturbance between missense variants in the LRR domain versus truncating loss-of-function variants across expanded multi-center LRRC7 cohorts?
